newsitem.title: GERMANY: German office accepts Allianz takeover plan.
newsitem.headline: German office accepts Allianz takeover plan.

text.p: Germany's cartel office said on Tuesday it had approved plans by Europe's largest insurance company, Allianz AG Holding, to take over insurer Vereinte Holding AG and loan insurer Hermes.
Allianz surprised analysts in July with plans to take over Vereinte fully in a complex deal arranged with Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG.
The deal followed unsuccessful attempts by Allianz to sell off a stake held in Vereinte.
A spokeswoman for the cartel office confirmed that approval for the moves had been given, but declined to give any further details.
In Munich, a spokesman for Allianz commented, "This means we can proceed in integrating these two companies in a way which will bring benefits for our customers."

The intricate deal with Munich Re divided up control of the country's two largest health insurers. DKV, which Munich Re controls as a result of the deal, is also Europe's largest private health insurance group.
Analysts had earlier expected Allianz to sell off Vereinte, which it acquired from Swiss Re in 1994.
